headline: U.S. defense company Lockheed Martin and Germany's Rheinmetall have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) at the NATO Industry Forum, held on the sidelines of the alliance's summit in Ankara, to establish a joint production line for ATACMS ballistic missiles. The guided missiles will be manufactured at Rheinmetall's artillery plant in Unterlüß, northern Germany, making it the first ATACMS production facility outside the United States. Expansion of the site is already underway, with production of rocket motors and other missile components expected to begin in 2027. Rheinmetall estimates the facility will be capable of meeting European and Ukrainian demand for 600–800 ATACMS missiles annually. Separately, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte announced that several other U.S. defense companies are also pursuing initiatives to manufacture American weapon systems in Europe. “This will enable us to produce or support key U.S. weapon systems here in Europe, including Abrams tanks, AMRAAM air defense missiles, ATACMS missiles, Barracuda 500M, Small Diameter Bombs, and Stinger missiles,” he said.
